name: Yonex Exbolt 68 10m Badminton String (7 Colors)
lines: Brought to you by the @Badminton Serve

While EXBOLT 63 focuses on speed and 65 on control, EXBOLT 68 prioritizes power. It features FORGED FIBER technology for durability and repulsion, with an oval shape to enhance smash power and reduce fiber deformation. The thinner gauge maintains repulsion while adding shuttle hold. An additional coating, Elasticity Outer, improves control. Despite its 0.68mm gauge, EXBOLT 68 is the most durable string in Yonex's lineup.
High Repulsion, Great Durability, Hitting Sound, And Excellent Control

Introducing a brand-new addition to the EXBOLT string series, EXBOLT 68. The EXBOLT series is renowned for their superior repulsion and durability but with the new EXBOLT 68 we upped the power. This new addition will be available on March 8, 2024.

Similar to the EXBOLT 63 and the EXBOLT 65, the EXBOLT 68 is constructed with a proprietary material called FORGED FIBER which combines durability and quick repulsion. While thinner strings tend to have higher repulsion, there has always been the issue of low durability. FORGED FIBER was developed to solve this very issue. Ordinary nylon had a limit to the strength of its fibers, which is why Yonex reconstructed the fibers on a molecular level to build stronger bonds for lasting durability.

For the new EXBOLT 68, the FORGED FIBER shape has been altered from a circular pattern to an oval pattern. This new shape limits the deformation of the fiber on impact increasing overall smash power. By using an extremely durable material, the thickness of the string is reduced to improve repulsion without compromising durability. The thinner gauge compared to conventional durable strings add the repulsive feel while retaining the characteristic shuttle hold of thick gauge strings.

To increase overall control an extra coating, the Elasticity Outer, is added for increased shuttle hold. The Elasticity Outer is a coating with enhanced flexibility achieved by applying NANOALLOY technology to nylon. The result is a combination of quick repulsion, durability, and control.

With the introduction of the EXBOLT 63 we bred speed, we followed this up with a slightly more control focused string in the form of EXBOLT 65. With this new addition, we introduced a power centric string to the series. Despite its 0.68mm gauge, the EXBOLT 68 becomes the most durable string in our entire string line-up. EXBOLT now offers an option for each playstyle.

FORGED FIBER, a material developed from a fiber with high intermolecular bonding strength, durability, and heat resistance, which is also used in the forging of aircraft tires. Impurities are removed during the manufacturing process, and by stretching the material many times longer than the original material, the strength of this FORGED FIBER is greatly increased.
The FORGED FIBER is molded in an oval shape rather than the usual circle. This oval shape limits the deformation of the fiber on impact increasing overall smash power.
The Elasticity Outer is a coating with enhanced flexibility achieved by applying NANOALLOY technology to nylon. The result is a combination of quick repulsion, durability, and control.

The BG80’s multifilament nylon core is engineered for high repulsion — storing and releasing energy rapidly on impact to drive the shuttle off the string bed with maximum force on smashes and overhead clears.

Rigid Vectran fibers wrap the core to limit string deformation on contact. This stiff outer layer locks in power transfer, reduces energy loss, and produces the BG80’s characteristic loud, heavy hitting sound.

The combination of a high-intensity core and rigid outer wrap creates a stiff, direct string bed. Players feel immediate, solid feedback on every shot — particularly on full-swing smashes and back-court drives where power transfer is the priority.

At 0.68mm, the BG80 sits in the mid-gauge range — thicker than ultra-thin performance strings like the EXBOLT 63, which means better durability for hard hitters while still delivering high repulsion on aggressive shots.

The BG80 produces a loud, heavy sound on contact — a direct result of the rigid Vectran outer wrap limiting string movement. Players who prefer strong auditory feedback on smashes and clears will find the BG80’s sound profile satisfying and confidence-building.
Yonex manufactures the BG80 in Japan, applying the same quality standards used across their premium string lineup to ensure consistent gauge, tension retention, and performance across every set.

The BG80 is a power-amplification string. It works best when paired with rackets where raw smash force is the primary goal, or as a counter-balance string to soften overly fast or thin-feeling setups.
Locks in the head-heavy smash power of these frames. The stiff BG80 bed transfers maximum force from the frame’s mass into the shuttle on full-swing smashes.
Adds weight and solidity to head-light frames that can feel too fast or thin. The BG80’s stiff bed gives back-court substance to speed-oriented rackets.
Pairs with the 88S Pro’s net-attack geometry to add raw power on cross-court drives and mid-court interceptions where a stiff string bed accelerates the shuttle.
Softens the Arcsaber 11 Tour’s control-oriented setup with added repulsion — useful for players who want more pop on clears without switching to a more aggressive frame.
Adds back-court power to medium-flex frames that benefit from a stiffer string bed to compensate for their softer flex profile on full-swing shots.
Balances the 77 Tour’s medium-flex feel with a stiffer string bed, giving players more direct power transfer on smashes without changing the frame’s comfortable swing weight.
Best For: Heavy Smashers, Back-Court Doubles Players & Players Who Want a Solid, Stiff String Bed

The BG80 is the right choice for players who prioritize raw power over touch or spin. Its stiff, rigid feel rewards aggressive back-court players who rely on full-swing smashes, powerful clears, and hard drives. It’s particularly well suited to head-heavy Astrox users who want to maximize the frame’s smash potential, and to doubles back-court players who need consistent, loud power on every attack. Players who prefer a softer, more cushioned feel or who prioritize net play and deception will likely prefer a more flexible string like the EXBOLT 65 or SKYARC.

lines: Shred the air with an exhilarating and powerful sound with the world's thinnest string. Yonex Aerosonic is designed for players seeking high repulsion and a hard-hitting sound.
Outer: Special Braided High Polymer Nylon

Yonex Aerosonic is a decent badminton string with high repulsion power and control. It is best suited to someone with an advanced level of skill. Many doubles players prefer it because of its thinnest gauge size which adds intense repulsion. If you are a beginner or recreational player, string it at a lower tension for an expanded sweet spot.
Is Yonex Aerosonic durable at 0.61mm gauge?

Yonex Aerosonic is one of the thinnest badminton strings in the world. At 0.61mm gauge, many question its durability. However, the company has used "Compact Filled Structure" to reinforce the construction design and make it more durable. It makes the BGAS string more successful in competing with other thicker gauge options available on the market.
What is the Alternative to Yonex Aerosonic?

Yonex BG66 may be thicker with a 0.66mm gauge but it has a similar medium feeling like Yonex Aerosonic. If you want a thinner string with high repulsion power like Aerosonic, you can consider using Li-Ning - N61 or Ashaway ZyMax 62 Fire (0.62mm).

lines: Nanotechnology comes to Yonex's strings, the Nanogy 98 are high on durability, playability, and style. Available in light metallic gold, these strings make an impression on and off the court. Yonex's new badminton string, the Nanogy 98.

Yonex Nanogy 98 is a good badminton string when you need extra repulsion for your shots. It has the additional Compound Cup-Stack Carbon Nanotube coating that ensures better control. Remember durability and string tension loss can be issues that you will have to address especially if you are a beginner.
Yonex Nanogy 98 vs. BG80: Which one is Better?
If your priority is speed and durability, choose Yonex BG80. For repulsion and decent control, Yonex Nanogy 98 is the best option for you.

name: Yonex BG-80 Power Badminton String Set 10m
lines: Yonex BG 80 Power badminton string is a powerful option for hard hitters. The 0.68mm string is a combination of high-intensity nylon multifilament with Vectran™ which is five times stronger than steel. It has an outer coating of special braided high polymer nylon for additional repulsion and strength.

The Yonex BG 80 Power strings are preferred by badminton champs including Lakshya Sen, Yugo Kobayashi, and Takuro Hoki. If you enjoy an aggressive game like your favorite badminton player, the BG80P strings can be well suited to you.
Core: High-Intensity Nylon Multifilament with Vectran
Outer: Special Braided High Polymer Nylon
Yonex BG 80 or BG 80 Power: Which one is better?

Both are ideal for hard hitters who want a durable badminton racket string. The original Yonex BG80 has a hard feeling and is recommended for advanced players. The BG80 Power is more forgiving because of its softer feel. It allows for better control in addition to power. In terms of durability, BG80 Power wins the race.
BG80 Power Vs. Exbolt 63: Which one is more durable?

BG 80 Power has a gauge thickness of 0.68mm and Exbolt 63 is 0.63mm thick. BG 80 Power focuses on aggressive shots while Exbolt 63 focuses more on repulsion and speed. Exbolt 63 can be a bit stiff in comparison to BG80 Power.

name: Yonex BG65 Badminton String Set (10m)
lines: The Yonex BG65 10m badminton string is one of Yonex's most popular strings, known for its exceptional durability and consistent performance. Featuring a 0.70mm gauge with a special braided fiber construction, it provides a balanced combination of control, comfort, and repulsion. Ideal for beginners, intermediate, and club players, BG65 is perfect for regular training and matches, offering reliable playability and long-lasting tension retention.
Color: White, Black, Orange, Turquoise, Lavender
Outer: Special Braided High Polymer Nylon

Yonex BG65 is an all-around badminton string for players who want to prioritize durability. It is good for beginners and recreational players who want an affordable badminton string that does not lose string tension quickly. In addition to durability, it has a soft-hitting feel and decent repulsion power.
What are the Alternatives to Yonex BG65?
Yonex BG65 badminton string is a good choice for players who need durability. Similar badminton strings include Yonex Nanogy 95, Ashaway Zymax 69 Fire, Nydhi NS700 XT, and Li-Ning No. 7 Classic.
Yonex BG65 vs. BG66 vs. BG80: Which one is Better?

All three strings are different in terms of the players they cater to. Yonex BG65 is often preferred by beginners who want a durable string. It is also a decent choice for hard hitters. Yonex BG66 has a thinner gauge size of 0.66m and focuses on repulsion, instead of durability. And, Yonex BG80 is designed for quick repulsion and heavy smashes. It has a gauge of 0.68mm so it is more durable than BG66 but less than Yonex BG65.

yonex bg65 ti has an extra coating of compound titanium hydride. it adds to the durability racket and offers a hard feeling upon shuttlecock contact. on contrary soft feel.

name: Victor VBS-66 Badminton String Set 10m - White
lines: Victor's string range is used by players at the top of the world game, and the VBS-66 is the control string in that line. At 0.66mm it is a mid-gauge string wrapped with high-strength multifilament, which is what gives it its crisp hitting sound and its reputation for holding placement.
— produces the crisp, high-pitched hitting sound the VBS line is known for.
— keeps resilience and durability over a long stringing cycle.
— suited to players chasing placement rather than raw repulsion.

Victor rate the VBS-66 at 7 for control, 8 for durability, 9 for repulsion power and 7 for hitting sound. In practice that reads as a string with unusually good repulsion for its gauge, and enough durability that a club player is not restringing every fortnight.

Players underestimate how much of a racket's feel comes from the string. A control-oriented string at a sensible gauge lets you place a drop shot where you meant to, and the multifilament wrap gives you the audible feedback that tells you when you have caught it right.
A well-balanced control string with more repulsion than its gauge suggests. A sound choice for club players who want placement without giving up durability.

name: Hundred JP58 Magnite Badminton String - Formula 1 Red 0.58mm/10m Set (HBAA-4M009-4)
lines: The Hundred JP58 Magnite is an ultra-thin 0.58mm badminton string built for attacking players who want rapid shuttle speed, precise control and sharp feedback from the string bed. A super-strength nylon multifilament core is wrapped in a highly resistant nylon monofilament outer layer and finished with a high-power complex elastic resin coating, giving exceptional repulsion with a crisp, satisfying response at impact. Supplied as a 10m single-racket set in Formula 1 Red.
— maximises repulsion and shuttle speed for quicker drives and sharper net exchanges.
— delivers responsive energy transfer so you generate pace without losing control.
Highly resistant nylon monofilament outer layer
— adds durability and keeps the string bed stable under heavy play.
— optimises energy return at impact for faster shots and a livelier feel.
— exceptional shuttle rebound for aggressive clears and rapid front-court play.
— precise string-bed feedback for accurate placement on smashes, drives and tight angles.
— damps vibration to reduce arm fatigue during long sessions.
— the standard length for one restring, ready to go.

On court, the JP58 Magnite feels distinctly aggressive. The thin gauge lets the shuttle spring off the bed with minimal effort, which suits players who rely on speed and placement to dominate rallies rather than sheer power. The multifilament core and monofilament outer layer combine into a responsive yet forgiving bed that holds consistent depth and timing even under pressure.

The resin coating amplifies energy return, giving punchier clears and quicker net exchanges without a dramatic loss of control. You still get precise touch for delicate drops, while retaining the high repulsion needed for fast drives and quick transitions. Tension stays predictable through extended rallies, so your rhythm and shot confidence hold as the pace escalates.
Faster shuttle speed and sharper attacking play from a thinner gauge.
Crisp, confidence-building feedback that helps you time your smashes.
Comfortable enough for long sessions thanks to strong shock absorption.
Tournament-grade performance in a convenient single-racket set.

The JP58 Magnite is a purpose-built string for players who attack with pace and precision. Its 0.58mm gauge, multifilament core and durable outer layer deliver explosive repulsion and crisp feedback while keeping comfort and control intact. If you play fast rallies, aggressive net play or heavy smashing and want a string that rewards speed, the JP58 Magnite is an outstanding choice. 🏸

name: Hundred JP66 Badminton String Set - Popsicle Orange (HBAA-2M156-5)
lines: The Hundred JP66 is a high-repulsion multifilament badminton string built for players who want power, a crisp hitting sound and a soft feel on the shuttle. This 10m set comes in Popsicle Orange, one of Hundred's brightest colourways, and suits attacking and all-round players stringing a single racket.
A middle-ground thickness balancing repulsion with string life.
Heat-resistant, high-intensity braided core for elasticity and feel.
Heat-resistant outer wrap that handles repeated hard contact.
Adds snapback and helps hold tension between sessions.
Bright, high-visibility colour in Hundred's JP66 range.

Hundred rate the JP66 10/10 for repulsion power, 10/10 for shock absorption and 10/10 for hitting sound, with 9/10 for both control and durability. In play that translates into a lively, powerful string bed that still cushions the shuttle on touch shots — the softer profile takes the sting out of hard contact, which helps on the arm over long sessions, while the crisp acoustic feedback makes clean strikes easy to feel. It is a natural fit for attacking singles and doubles players who want smash speed without a harsh, boardy response.
Explosive repulsion for smashes and deep clears.
Soft, cushioned feel that reduces harsh vibration.

The Hundred JP58 Magnite badminton string is a premium 0.58mm gauge string set designed for attacking players who demand rapid shuttle speed, precise control, and outstanding feedback. Built around a robust nylon multifilament core with a high-durability nylon monofilament outer layer and a high power elastic resin coating, the JP58 Magnite delivers exceptional repulsion and crisp on-impact feel. Targeted at intermediate to advanced players, it excels in fast rallies, net pressure, and aggressive shotmaking, while maintaining comfort and stability across long sessions. This is a true performance upgrade for players seeking tournament-ready performance from their string bed.
Ultra-thin 0.58mm gauge: Maximises repulsion and shuttle speed, translating into quicker drives and sharper net exchanges on consistent contact.
Nylon Multifilament Core: Delivers a lively, lively feel with responsive energy transfer, helping you generate pace without sacrificing control.
Outer Nylon Monofilament Layer: Enhances durability and stability under heavy play, so string bed remains consistent across rallies.
High Power Elastic Resin Coating: Optimises energy return at impact for faster shots and lively response, while smoothing contact for better feel.
10 metres in length: Standard single-racket length streamlines stringing preparation and accommodates most racket specs.
Repulsion Power: 10/10: Exceptional shuttle rebound, supporting aggressive clears and rapid front-court play.
Control: 9/10: Precise string-bed feedback enabling accurate placement on smashes, drives, and tight angles.
Shock Absorption: 9/10: Damps vibration to reduce arm fatigue and improve comfort during long sessions.
Durability: 7.5/10: Balanced for high-performance play without excessive need for frequent restringing.
Hitting Sound: 10/10: Crisp, satisfying feedback on contact that helps with timing and shot confidence.
Player Level: Intermediate / Advanced: Engineered for players who string for speed and attack, rather than for sheer durability alone.
Recommended Use: Tournament / Attacking Play / Fast Rallies: Optimised for aggressive styles and rapid-fire exchanges at the baseline and at the net.

On court, the JP58 Magnite delivers a distinctly aggressive feel. The 0.58mm gauge sands away some of the hesitation you might experience with thicker strings, allowing the shuttle to spring off the bed with minimal effort—ideal for players who rely on speed and placement to dominate rallies. The combination of a nylon multifilament core and a high-durability nylon monofilament outer layer creates a responsive yet forgiving string bed, enabling consistent depth and sharp timing even under pressure. The resin coating further amplifies energy return, giving you punchier clears and quicker net exchanges without a dramatic loss of control.

Together, these elements translate into a string that rewards aggressive play with confident feedback. Players will notice precise touch for delicate drop shots, while still enjoying the high repulsion needed for fast drives and quick transitions at the net. The JP58 Magnite maintains stable string tension during extended rallies, helping you keep your rhythm and trust in shot execution when the pace escalates. For tournament play or hard-hitting practice sessions, this string beds in quickly and remains predictable through long, demanding sessions.

Produced from Ashaway’s revolutionary BETA Polymer raw material, ZyMax® Fire products are the first badminton strings to utilize this new polymer technology. All ZyMax® Fire strings incorporate BETA fibers with ZyWeaVe technology to provide:
· Incredible knot and loop strength resulting in optimum toughness and durability
· Sensational elasticity and dynamic stiffness resulting in excellent feel and repulsion
· Maximum tension stability resulting in consistent, reliable performance

ZyMax 66 Fire is a 0.66mm string and is produced in two unique designs tailored specifically for players at the high performance end of the player spectrum. ZyMax 66 Fire is designed for precise shotmaking and is recommended for players that like a stiffer, more control-oriented string bed. ZyMax 66 Fire is designed for maximum power and repulsion and is recommended for players that like a softer, more powerful string bed. Both of the ZyMax 66 Fire models have superior toughness, tension stability and durability at all tensions when compared to all existing micro gauge badminton strings on the market.

name: Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String
lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String:

Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String occupies a unique position in the string market — it is the only string in Victor's Durability Series that simultaneously achieves 9/10 repulsion. This combination should not be possible by conventional string physics: durability strings use thicker construction that limits repulsion, and high-repulsion strings use thinner construction that limits durability. The VBS 69 Nano resolves this tension through nanotechnology special weaving — at 0.69mm, the nano-bonded fibre structure snaps back faster and more energetically than standard thick string construction while maintaining the fibre volume needed for durability-tier longevity. The result is a string that belongs in the Durability Series by construction, yet performs in the repulsion tier that 0.66mm strings typically occupy.

Victor's own categorisation and recommendation framework confirms exactly this positioning. In VICTOR LAB, the VBS 69 Nano is consistently recommended alongside power attacking rackets — the Thruster TK-9000/9900 (heavy power), the Jetspeed JS-10/11 (fast attacking), and the HX-800/990 (aggressive control-attacking). These are not beginners' or all-court rackets — they are attacking specialists' tools. Victor's pairing of the VBS 69 Nano with these rackets reflects their engineering intent: this is a durability string that matches the performance demands of aggressive attacking play, something the VBS 70's lower repulsion cannot deliver to the same standard.

The feel honest complexity requires addressing directly. Victor officially classifies the VBS 69 Nano as soft. Victor's own VICTOR LAB description, however, states that it has "a slightly harder feeling compared with VBS-70." Independent expert reviewer CK Yew's practical testing corroborates this: he found the 69 to feel stiffer than the 70 and stated he would swap their official feel ratings. The consensus from primary sources is consistent: VBS 69 Nano is medium to soft — firmer than the genuinely soft VBS 70, but comfortable enough for the "extremely easy-to-manage" description Victor applies to it. Indian players stepping from BG65 or Li-Ning No. 7 (both 0.70mm soft-feel strings) should expect the VBS 69 Nano to feel slightly more demanding on contact — which most experienced club players report as an improvement, not a drawback.

Expert stringer ERR KL notes the VBS 69 Nano is not widely chosen by Malaysian players — most opt for either thinner repulsion strings (VBS 63, VBS 66 Nano) or the full 0.70mm VBS 70 for durability. The VBS 69 Nano is a niche but well-engineered choice for the specific player who wants maximum durability-tier repulsion at thick-gauge construction — a rare requirement that the nanotechnology weaving delivers uniquely in this gauge.
String Character Breakdown of Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String:

0.69mm sits one step thinner than the VBS 70's 0.70mm and one step thicker than the VBS 66 Nano's 0.66mm. This placement in the gauge spectrum is deliberate — the 0.01mm reduction from 0.70mm alone would produce minimal improvement in repulsion over a standard VBS 70. It is the nanotechnology weaving that converts this marginal gauge reduction into the 9/10 repulsion rating. At 0.69mm, the string still carries enough fibre volume for durability-tier longevity while the nano construction produces repulsion that far exceeds what conventional 0.69mm construction would achieve.
Core — High-Intensity Nylon with Nanotechnology Weaving:

High-intensity nylon (stronger per-fibre grade than standard nylon) combined with nanotechnology special weaving is the construction combination that makes the VBS 69 Nano's dual 9/10 rating possible. The special weaving technique creates tightly bonded molecular connections between fibres — more energetically efficient energy storage and faster snap-back than conventional weaving at this gauge. Victor's VICTOR LAB notes "great elasticity remains" — the nanotechnology preserves elasticity in a gauge tier where standard strings sacrifice it for durability.
Nanotechnology Special Weaving — The Dual Performance Engine:

Unlike the VBS 66 Nano's Nano-Tec (which primarily targets tension degradation resistance) or Li-Ning's 3D Knit (which targets fibre interlocking for durability), the VBS 69 Nano's nanotechnology weaving serves both performance dimensions simultaneously — maximising elastic snap-back speed (repulsion) and structural bonding integrity (durability) through the same construction process. This is the engineering innovation that allows the string to bridge the repulsion-durability divide that conventional strings cannot cross.
Feel — Medium to Soft (Practically Firmer than VBS 70):

Officially classified as soft, but in practice it plays slightly firmer than the VBS 70. The VBS 69 Nano's firmer feel is attributed to the nanotechnology weaving's tighter fibre bonding — the string bed is slightly stiffer on deformation and returns slightly faster. The feel remains comfortable and manageable — Victor accurately describes it as "extremely easy-to-manage" — but players expecting VBS 70-equivalent softness should calibrate expectations accordingly.

Like the VBS 70, the VBS 69 Nano has a coating that provides abrasion protection at cross-string notch points and contributes to the string's satisfying hitting sound (8/10). The coating also gives the string a slight surface grip that assists control on placement shots and net exchanges.
Performance Ratings — Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String:

Exceptional for a durability string — nanotechnology weaving at 0.69mm delivers repulsion equal to VBS 63 and far above VBS 70's 7–8/10. The most repulsive string in Victor's Durability Series by a significant margin. Players stepping from BG65 or VBS 70 will feel an immediate, meaningful increase in shuttle speed from the string bed.

Good control for its gauge tier. The slightly firmer feel provides useful directional feedback on attacking shots — Victor recommends pairing it with attacking rackets specifically because the firmer feel suits the deliberate, forceful contact of power play. 0.69mm gauge provides a slightly larger sweet spot than 0.65mm alternatives, adding a margin of error tolerance on off-centre attacks.

Near-maximum durability — 0.69mm gauge plus nanotechnology construction together provide fibre volume and bonding integrity that withstands repeated high-impact attacking shots. Victor specifically states the VBS 69 Nano is "built for repeated high-impact play." For regular advanced club players at 24–26 lbs: 4–8 weeks is typical. At 26–28 lbs: 3–5 weeks. Meaningfully longer lifespan than VBS 66 Nano while delivering the same repulsion rating.

Medium to soft — firmer than VBS 70, softer and more comfortable than performance tier strings. Hitting sound is 8/10 — clearer and higher-pitched than the VBS 70 despite being in the same durability tier. The nanotechnology construction's faster snap-back adds energy to the contact feel that makes each shot feel more decisive than VBS 70 at equivalent tension.
Tension Guide for Victor VBS 69 Nano — Indian Courts:

The most accessible and forgiving range for the Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String. At 22–24 lbs, the nanotechnology repulsion is clearly expressed — players accustomed to BG65 or VBS 70 at similar tensions will feel the VBS 69 Nano's meaningfully better shuttle speed. Good for players making their first step up from 0.70mm thick strings toward better repulsion performance.

The recommended range for attacking players pairing the Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String with power or speed attacking rackets. Victor's pairing recommendations for JS-10, JS-11, TK-9000, and MX-80 rackets at this tension range reflect the string's ideal operating environment — tight enough for directional precision, responsive enough for the 9/10 repulsion to translate into attacking shuttle speed.

The upper range recommended by Victor (22–29 lbs). ERR KL's stringer uses 27 lbs for casual games; competitive power players may go to 28–29 lbs for maximum response. Victor specifically notes the Durability Series strings are "best paired with higher tension (around 28 lbs) to maintain a strong response" — the VBS 69 Nano's nanotechnology construction handles this tension range while maintaining its dual repulsion-durability profile.

The VBS 69 Nano performs consistently in India's warm, humid conditions. The nanotechnology bonding helps maintain consistent tension and feel across varying temperature and humidity conditions better than conventional durability strings. Players in coastal cities who play in both air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned venues will find the Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String more consistent between environments than standard thick strings.
String Finder — Is Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String Right for You?
Attacking Player Who Needs Durability-Tier Longevity But Wants Better Repulsion Than VBS 70:

The VBS 69 Nano's core audience. You play aggressively and break strings relatively frequently — VBS 66 Nano's 3–6 week lifespan is not enough. But VBS 70's 7–8/10 repulsion feels dead compared to your technique. The Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String gives you 9/10 repulsion that lasts 4–8 weeks at club tension.
BG65 or Yonex BG65 Titanium User Who Wants a Victor Alternative:

ERR KL specifically recommends the Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String as the upgrade for BG65 users. Same durability tier, marginally thinner gauge, nanotechnology construction producing significantly more repulsion. "It will feel much better in comparison" is their direct assessment.
Player Pairing With a Power Attacking Racket:

Victor's own racket-string pairing guide repeatedly pairs the Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String with their most aggressive attacking rackets (JS-10, JS-11, TK-9000, MX-80, HX-800). If you play a power-attacking racket and want a string that matches its intent while providing durability, the VBS 69 Nano is Victor's official recommendation.
Player Choosing Between VBS 69 Nano and VBS 66 Nano:

VBS 66 Nano (0.66mm, High Resilience): thinner, slightly more repulsion on day one, Nano-Tec tension retention, better control from textured surface. VBS 69 Nano (0.69mm, Durability): thicker, 9/10 repulsion equal to VBS 66 Nano, better durability (9/10 vs 8/10), slightly firmer feel. Choose Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String for better longevity at equal repulsion; choose VBS 66 Nano for better control and Nano-Tec tension retention.
Playing Style Guide for Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String:

Ideal Match. 9/10 repulsion with 9/10 durability — the only Victor string that achieves both simultaneously. Victor specifically recommends this string for attacking rackets and attacking players. Power smashers who want strings that survive their intensity while delivering full attacking repulsion should choose Victor VBS 69 Nano Badminton String over VBS 70.

Moderate Match. 7/10 control is solid but the VBS 66 Nano's textured surface provides better shuttle grip for precision net shots. For control-first players who still want thick-gauge durability, the VBS 69 Nano is a reasonable choice — firmer feel provides decent placement feedback.

Good Match for intermediate all-court players who want durability with better repulsion than VBS 70. For true beginners, VBS 70's genuinely soft feel and maximum durability are more appropriate. VBS 69 Nano suits the intermediate-to-advanced all-court player who trains frequently and needs strings that last.

Attacking durability bridge — highest repulsion in Durability Series, nanotechnology weaving
Softest feel, all-level user-friendly — Thermotech Nylon Resin

name: Victor VBS 61 Badminton String
lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Victor VBS 61 Badminton String:

Victor VBS 61 Badminton String is Victor's most extreme performance string — 0.61mm ultra-thin, maximum repulsion, made in Japan, and positioned as a direct competitor to the Yonex Aerosonic, which previously held a near-monopoly on the 0.61mm segment. For context on what 0.61mm means in practical terms: it is 0.04mm thinner than the VBS 63, 0.05mm thinner than the VBS 66 Nano, and 0.09mm thinner than the VBS 70. On paper these are tiny numbers. In practice, the reduction in fibre count from 0.66mm to 0.61mm produces a perceptible jump in shuttle speed and a sharper, more immediate contact feel — at the cost of a proportional reduction in durability and a smaller effective sweet spot.

One important point for every Victor VBS string purchase: the VBS number directly tells you the gauge. Victor VBS 61 Badminton String = 0.61mm. VBS 63 = 0.63mm. VBS 66 Nano = 0.66mm. VBS 70 = 0.70mm. This transparent naming convention is unique among major brands — Yonex's BG numbers do not reflect gauge (BG65 is not 0.65mm; Exbolt 63 happens to be 0.63mm but this is coincidental), and Li-Ning's No. series gives no gauge information at all. When comparing Victor VBS strings, the number is the first and most direct way to understand the string's fundamental character.

The VBS 61's braided outer layer is the construction distinction that separates it from the Aerosonic at the same 0.61mm gauge. The Aerosonic uses a hi-polymer braided construction that produces an ultra-crisp, borderline harsh contact feel at the absolute performance limit. The VBS 61's braided outer layer produces a medium feel — still crisp and fast, but with slightly more shuttle grip that contributes to better net shot control and touch on delicate placements. For professional and advanced players who find the Aerosonic's contact too harsh or too unforgiving on net shots, the Victor VBS 61 Badminton String may provide the preferred balance at the same ultra-thin gauge.

The high-strength core construction is Victor's explicit claim of improved durability over previous 0.61mm alternatives — which, given the Aerosonic's well-documented fragility, is a meaningful target. Whether this translates to meaningfully longer string life in practice is something players will discover at their specific tension and playing intensity. At 0.61mm, "improved durability" is a relative term — the Victor VBS 61 Badminton String is still a fragile string that advanced players should expect to restring frequently.
String Character Breakdown of Victor VBS 61 Badminton String:

Victor's thinnest standard string — the same gauge as the Yonex Aerosonic. At 0.61mm, the string bed deforms maximally under impact and snaps back at the highest possible velocity for a given tension — producing the strongest repulsion effect of any Victor string. The ultra-thin gauge also means fewer fibres per cross-section: the trade-off for maximum repulsion is the lowest durability in the Victor range and the most demanding feel profile for players transitioning from thicker strings.

Victor specifically highlights the "new high-strength multifilament" in the Victor VBS 61 Badminton String — indicating a material and construction upgrade from earlier Victor ultra-thin strings. High-strength nylon has better fatigue resistance per fibre than standard nylon, partially compensating for the reduced fibre count at 0.61mm. This core construction is the primary carrier of the string's repulsion energy — the multifilament fibres collectively deform and snap back on impact to launch the shuttle.

The braided outer provides two specific benefits at 0.61mm. First, it adds modest structural reinforcement to the thin string body, contributing to the improved durability claim. Second, the braided texture creates a slight surface roughness that provides shuttle grip on contact — enabling better control on net shots, drops, and slices than a completely smooth outer would at this gauge. The medium feel classification of the VBS 61 (compared to the ultra-harsh feel of smooth-outer ultra-thin strings) reflects this braided outer's contribution.
High Resilience Series — Maximum Snap-Back Speed:

The VBS 61 belongs to Victor's High Resilience string series — strings engineered specifically for the fastest possible string bed recovery after impact. High resilience means the string returns to its original position faster after deforming under shuttle contact, expelling the shuttle with more force and in a shorter contact time than lower resilience alternatives. For players who play fast, attacking badminton, this faster snap-back translates to higher shuttle velocity for equivalent swing speed.

Despite the ultra-thin gauge, the VBS 61 is classified as medium feel rather than hard — the braided outer's surface character and the high-strength multifilament core's elastic properties combine to produce a feel that is fast and crisp but not as unforgiving as the hardest-feel ultra-thin alternatives. The medium feel makes the VBS 61 more accessible to a slightly wider player profile than the Aerosonic's harsher contact.

Japan-manufactured badminton strings undergo the most rigorous manufacturing quality control. For an ultra-thin 0.61mm string where dimensional consistency between individual filaments directly affects both performance and durability, Japan manufacturing is a genuine specification advantage over strings manufactured to lower quality control standards.
Performance Ratings — Victor VBS 61 Badminton String:

lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Li-Ning No 7 Boost Badminton String:

Li-Ning No 7 Boost Badminton String is the premium durability option in the No. 7 family — the string you choose when you want everything the original No. 7 offers, plus the additional construction assurance of 3D Knit technology. In the parallel No. 1 family, the "Boost" designation brought a new third layer (elastic resin coating) that fundamentally changed the string's feel. In the No. 7 family, the Boost is more evolutionary — it adds 3D Knit to the original's already strong Deep-Re-Dipping foundation, creating a string where durability is engineered from two independent angles simultaneously: polymer saturation from outside (Deep-Re-Dipping) and fibre interlocking from within (3D Knit).

Understanding why two durability technologies together matter more than one requires understanding how strings typically fail. Most string performance degradation happens through two mechanisms: fibre separation (fibres within the multifilament core progressively pull apart from each other under repeated impact, causing the string to lose stiffness and response) and polymer breakdown (the coating and outer nylon degrade from abrasion, moisture, and UV exposure over time). Deep-Re-Dipping addresses the second mechanism — polymer saturation resists external breakdown. 3D Knit addresses the first — three-dimensional fibre interlocking resists internal fibre separation. The No. 7 Boost attacks both failure modes simultaneously.

The practical implication for Indian players is straightforward: the Li-Ning No 7 Boost Badminton String holds its playing characteristics most consistently over time. At week eight or ten of a string's life — when an original No. 7 has experienced some fibre separation and slight feel change — the Boost's 3D Knit construction means the fibres are still more cohesively bonded, maintaining a closer-to-day-one response. For Indian players who restring seasonally or every 2–3 months, this extended consistency is the real-world value of the Boost premium.

In all other respects — feel, tension, playing character — the Li-Ning No 7 Boost Badminton String behaves identically to the original No. 7 on day one. Both are soft, forgiving, comfortable 0.70mm strings. The Boost's value is in the back half of its lifespan, not the first session. If your restringing interval is short (every 2–4 weeks), the original No. 7's durability is more than sufficient and the Boost premium is hard to justify. If your interval is long (every 2–6 months), the Boost is the better investment per string set.

Distributes impact stress more evenly across the string's cross-section, reduces local stress concentration that causes premature breakage, and maintains more consistent playing feel as the string ages. Works alongside Deep-Re-Dipping to address the two primary failure modes of string degradation simultaneously.

The same Deep-Re-Dipping process as the original No. 7 — repeated polymer immersion fills micro-gaps between fibres, prevents external moisture absorption, and dramatically extends string life. lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String:

Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String is the durability benchmark of Li-Ning's string range — and it earns that position not through gauge alone but through Deep-Re-Dipping: a manufacturing process that polymer-saturates the string's fibre structure to a depth and density that standard string production cannot replicate. The result is a 0.70mm string that outlasts most alternatives at equivalent gauge, stays playable longer between restrings, and holds tension better in India's humid playing conditions. At 10/10 for durability in Li-Ning's own rating — shared only by the No. 7 Boost and No. 7 Rebound in the family — the Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String is the string to choose when longevity is the primary requirement.

The China National Team's continued use of the Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String for training reflects a principle that many Indian club players underestimate: durability strings are not just for beginners. Professional players train for 5–9 hours daily and go through enormous string volume. The Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String gives them reliable, consistent feel for training without the cost and frequency of constantly restringing performance strings. The string's soft feel does not penalise professional technique at lower training tensions — it actually serves the deliberate, placement-focused training style that elite players use. Some advanced Malaysian club players specifically string the Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String at 27–29 lbs precisely because its non-elastic, controlled feel suits their technical, deliberate shot style.

The compound nylon hit-absorbing coating is the feel specification that distinguishes the No. 7's playing character. Where Yonex BG65 has a firmer, more utilitarian feel, the No. 7's coating provides a cushioned softness on contact — comfortable across extended training sessions and gentle on the elbow and shoulder for players who are susceptible to arm fatigue. For Indian players who play long sessions in humid conditions, the No. 7's comfort profile is a genuine advantage over harder alternatives at the same durability tier.

One observation from expert stringers is notable for Indian players: the No. 7's surface has a slightly less dry texture than equivalent Yonex strings at 0.70mm. This moistness of the surface coating contributes to better abrasion resistance where cross strings intersect — the primary breakage point of most strings. In India's humid conditions where string abrasion can accelerate, this slightly less-dry surface is a real durability advantage.
String Character Breakdown of Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String:

0.70mm is the standard durability gauge — more nylon fibre per cross-section means more resistance to impact stress, abrasion, and breakage than thinner strings. At 0.70mm, the string deforms slightly less on impact and snaps back more slowly than thin strings, producing lower repulsion but superior durability and comfort. For beginners, frequent players, and training contexts where string lifespan matters more than maximum shuttle speed, 0.70mm is the right choice.

High polymer nylon has greater elasticity, strength per fibre, and fatigue resistance than standard nylon — a meaningful material step up from basic multifilament cores. The high polymer designation means the nylon chains are longer and more densely organised at the molecular level, producing better mechanical properties without requiring additional gauge. This core material is the foundation of the No. 7's durability.

The No. 7's defining construction process. Repeated immersion in polymer solution during manufacturing fills the micro-gaps between fibres, creating a densely bonded, polymer-saturated string structure. This saturation does two things simultaneously: it prevents progressive fibre separation under impact (the primary cause of string performance degradation over time) and it reduces moisture absorption that causes strings to go dead faster in humid conditions. Expert stringers observe the result directly — the No. 7's surface has a less-dry texture than Yonex alternatives, reflecting the deeper polymer saturation within the string structure.

Heat-resistant specification ensures string properties remain consistent during extended play sessions where racket temperature rises. High-intensity nylon provides structural integrity and even tension distribution across the string bed. The outer protects the high polymer multifilament core from abrasion during play.

Applied over the nylon outer, the compound nylon coating provides the No. 7's characteristic soft feel on contact. The coating cushions the shuttle-string interface, reducing the impact transmitted to the player's arm. This hit-absorbing property is especially valuable for players with arm, elbow, or shoulder sensitivity — the No. 7 is the most comfortable Li-Ning string for extended play at any skill level.

The softest feel in the Li-Ning No. series. The compound nylon coating, 0.70mm gauge, and high polymer core combine to produce a cushioned, comfortable response on every shot. The shuttle dwell time is slightly longer than thin strings — the string bed compresses more before snapping back — giving a gentler, more forgiving contact that rewards consistent technique without punishing variation.
Performance Ratings — Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String:

Strong control rating for a durability string. Li-Ning's maximum durability rating. Deep-Re-Dipping polymer saturation, 0.70mm gauge, high polymer core, and heat-resistant construction combine for the longest string lifespan in Li-Ning's range. Soft and comfortable — the most arm-friendly feel in the Li-Ning No. series. The compound nylon hit-absorbing coating cushions every contact. Extended sessions are comfortable without the arm fatigue that harder-feel strings at higher tension can accumulate. Not the most exciting feel for players who prize crisp acoustic response, but reliably pleasant for players who want uncomplicated, comfortable play.
Tension Guide for Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String — Indian Courts:

The most forgiving tension range for the Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String. At 18–22 lbs, the string bed is at its most elastic, the sweet spot is largest, and the feel is softest. Beginners who are still developing consistent contact mechanics benefit from the maximum forgiveness at this range — miss-hits on a loosely strung Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String are far more forgiving than on tightly strung thin strings. The standard working range for most Indian club players using the Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String. Balanced between the string's forgiving softness and adequate control precision. At 22–24 lbs, the soft feel is most comfortable for long training sessions. At 24–26 lbs, placement precision improves without making the string demanding. This is the range where the No. 7's Deep-Re-Dipping tension retention benefit is most practically felt — the string stays near its strung tension noticeably longer than non-dipped alternatives.
Advanced Players Using No. 7 for Controlled Deliberate Play — 26–29 lbs:

Some advanced players specifically choose the Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String at higher tensions for its stable, non-bouncy feel. At 26–29 lbs, the No. 7 produces a controlled, deliberate response — the shuttle goes where technique directs it with minimal string-bed bounce influence. Advanced players who play technique-first badminton rather than relying on string repulsion often find this combination preferable for their style.

The polymer-saturated structure absorbs less moisture from the air — the string remains consistent in feel and tension between cool air-conditioned halls and warm outdoor or coastal courts. This is a meaningful practical advantage in India's varied playing conditions.

Far better investment than cheap no-brand strings that lack Deep-Re-Dipping's durability and go dead quickly.

For Indian club players who restring seasonally, the Li-Ning No 7 Badminton String is the honest recommendation.

Coaches who string multiple student rackets need a reliable, low-maintenance string. The No. 7's durability and consistent feel across extended use make it ideal for academy and coaching contexts where individual string quality is less important than consistent performance across a fleet of rackets.

lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String:

Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String is the third member of the No. 1 family and occupies a specific performance position between the original No. 1 (hard feel, best tension retention) and the No. 1 Boost (softer feel, best durability). At 0.65mm — the same gauge as the original No. 1 — the Rebound is engineered for elasticity and rebound response rather than hard feel or maximum durability. The defining characteristic is a springier, more lively string bed: the Rebound feels energetic on contact, with the shuttle appearing to spring from the string bed with greater elastic momentum than the direct, immediate departure of the original No. 1.

Understanding what "rebound" means as a string performance characteristic helps position this string correctly. The original No. 1's hard feel produces maximum directional control and crispness — the shuttle goes exactly where the swing directs it, with minimal elastic deviation. The Rebound's elasticity-optimised construction allows slightly more string bed deformation and a faster snap-back, adding an energetic, lively quality to the repulsion. This feel is closer to what Yonex BG66 Ultimax players describe as the string's "bounce" — but with the Rebound's better tension retention and sharper acoustic response that the No. 1 family is known for.

The acoustic signature is distinctive: the Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String produces a crisp, high-pitched sound with a slightly more resonant character than the original No. 1's dry crack. The elastic snap-back creates a brief additional string vibration after impact that contributes to a fuller, more satisfying hitting sound. Players who value acoustic feedback as part of their game confidence — and in Indian competitive club play, the sound of a well-hit shuttle is genuinely important to many players — will find the Rebound particularly satisfying.

Li-Ning India positions the Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String for "advanced players who demand high repulsion power and a sharp hitting sound" with a "moderate feel ideal for aggressive gameplay." This positioning aligns with the Rebound's place in the family: it is not the hardest or the softest, but the most energetically responsive — a string for players who want the No. 1 family's repulsion credentials with a feel that rewards fast, aggressive play with a lively, confident response from the string bed.
String Character Breakdown of Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String:

The same 0.65mm as the original No. 1 — placing the Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String firmly in the performance string tier with maximum repulsion potential from thinness. At 0.65mm, the string bed deforms more on impact and snaps back faster than thicker strings. The Rebound's elasticity construction amplifies this natural snap-back of thin strings into a more pronounced, energetic response.
Core — Heat Resistant High-Intensity Nylon Multifilament:

High-intensity nylon multifilament core providing the elastic foundation for repulsion. The Rebound's core construction is optimised for maximum elastic energy storage and release — the fibres deform more readily under impact and spring back faster, creating the lively feel that defines this string. Heat resistance ensures consistency across varying playing conditions.

High-intensity nylon outer protecting the core structure and providing the contact surface. The Rebound's outer maintains the direct nylon-to-shuttle contact that delivers a crisp acoustic response — no coating that would cushion the feel as the Boost's elastic resin does. This preserves the sharpness of the Rebound's hitting sound while the core construction provides the elastic energy.
Elasticity Optimisation — The Defining Rebound Property:

The Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String is specifically engineered for elastic response — the string's internal construction is calibrated to maximise the ratio of energy returned to the shuttle versus energy absorbed by the string. A more elastic string returns more of the impact energy to propel the shuttle rather than dissipating it as heat or vibration in the string body. This engineering focus produces the springier feel that distinguishes the Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String from the original No. 1's direct, hard-feel approach.

Li-Ning describes the Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String as providing excellent tension maintenance alongside its elasticity — an important qualifier for an elasticity-focused string. Some highly elastic strings sacrifice tension retention to achieve their lively feel. The Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String is positioned to maintain tension reasonably well, keeping the elastic response consistent over a longer period than BG66 Ultimax, whose tension loss progressively softens its feel within a few sessions.

Positioned between the original No. 1's hard profile and the Boost's soft profile. The Rebound has a crisp initial contact (from the direct nylon outer) with an elastic, springy snap-back (from the elasticity-optimised core). The combined effect is a feel that is more lively and energetic than the original No. 1's dry hardness, more precise and acoustically clear than the Boost's cushioned softness.
Performance Ratings — Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String:

Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String is of 0.65mm gauge and elasticity-optimised construction deliver very high repulsion. The elastic snap-back amplifies the natural repulsion of the thin gauge — shuttle leaves the string bed with energetic, lively momentum. Equal to the original No. 1 in repulsion power; the Rebound's elasticity focus makes the repulsion feel more pronounced and dynamic.

Good directional control from the thin gauge and direct nylon outer surface. The elastic snap-back adds slight shuttle dwell time compared to the original No. 1, which provides some additional shuttle grip on placement shots. Slightly less forensically precise than the original No. 1's hard feel on demanding control shots, but excellent for aggressive placement play.

At 0.65mm without the Boost's elastic resin coating durability enhancement, the Rebound's lifespan is comparable to the original No. 1. Expect 3–6 weeks for intermediate club players at 24–26 lbs; 2–3 weeks for advanced players at 27+ lbs. Better than BG66 Ultimax at this gauge. Not a durability string — the Boost is the better choice for players who prioritise longevity.

Medium-crisp and distinctly lively — the Rebound's defining quality. Energetic, springy response with a satisfying, resonant hitting sound. The elastic snap-back makes every contact feel decisive and dynamic. The most acoustically satisfying member of the No. 1 family for players who value the hitting sound as part of their game confidence. More pleasant to play extended sessions on than the original No. 1's hard feel.
Tension Guide for Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String — Indian Courts:

The Rebound's elastic response is most noticeable at lower tensions where string deformation is greater. At 22–25 lbs, the springy, lively feel is at its most pronounced — a significant step up from the feel of 0.70mm strings at the same tension. Good for players transitioning from thick strings who want to experience the Rebound's elastic character before moving to higher tension.

The optimal tension for most intermediate-to-advanced players using the Rebound. The elastic snap-back remains lively while placement precision improves. Acoustic response is at its clearest at this range — the Rebound's resonant hitting sound is fully expressed at 25–27 lbs.

The Rebound maintains its elastic character better at higher tensions than might be expected from an elasticity-focused string. Tension maintenance aids this — the string's playing feel does not degrade as quickly as BG66 Ultimax's does at similar tensions. At 27–29 lbs, the Rebound provides excellent precision alongside its lively elastic response.
Do not exceed 30 lbs. Always verify racket tension ceiling before stringing.

BG66 Ultimax Player Who Wants Better Tension Retention:

The Rebound's elastic feel is the closest in the No. 1 family to BG66 Ultimax's lively bounce — but with better tension retention. If the BG66 Ultimax's softening within days of stringing frustrates you but you love its elastic response, the Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String is the natural upgrade.
Player Between No. 1 and No. 1 Boost on Feel Preference:

You find the original No. 1 too hard but the Boost too soft. The Rebound's medium-crisp feel occupies the middle ground — more elastic than the original, more defined and acoustically crisp than the Boost.
Doubles Player Who Wants Thin-Gauge Responsiveness:

The Rebound's lively elastic response suits fast doubles exchanges where energetic repulsion from the string bed assists quick transitions. The 0.65mm thinness provides the repulsion for fast drives and net attacks; the elasticity provides the responsive feel for rapid rally continuity.

The Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String produces the most satisfying and resonant hitting sound in the No. 1 family — the elastic snap-back creates a fuller, more resonant crack than the original No. 1's dry hardness or the Boost's cushioned impact. For players who use the hitting sound as a performance indicator, the Rebound delivers the most satisfying acoustic experience in the No. 1 range.
Playing Style Guide for Li-Ning No 1 Rebound Badminton String:

Good Match. 0.65mm gauge and elasticity optimisation provide high repulsion for smash power. The lively elastic feel makes powerful smashes feel energetic and explosive. For maximum hard-feel smash precision, the original No. 1 is marginally better; for lively explosive smash feel, the Rebound is excellent.

Good Match. Thin gauge provides good placement precision. The elastic snap-back adds slight shuttle dwell for touch-shot control. The Rebound sits between the hard precision of the original No. 1 and the softer touch of the Boost — good for players who play a mixed control and power game rather than purely one or the other.

Good Match. Medium-crisp feel is the most versatile in the No. 1 family for all-court play. The elastic snap-back assists defensive lifts and repulsion on quick exchanges. The lively string bed feel makes the Rebound more comfortable over extended all-court sessions than the original No. 1's hard profile.

lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Li-Ning No 1 Badminton String:

The Li-Ning No 1 Badminton String is the most played string in China's national badminton programme — and that pedigree runs deep. Fu Hai Feng, PV Sindhu, and Kidambi Srikanth have all used it at world-class competitive level. This is not incidental: the No. 1's combination of 0.65mm thinness, hard contact feel, high repulsion power, crisp acoustic response, and superior tension retention makes it a genuine alternative to the Yonex BG66 Ultimax in the Indian competitive club market — and in the specific area of tension retention, it is meaningfully better.

The tension retention distinction is worth explaining precisely because it is the most practically important difference between the No. 1 and its closest Yonex equivalent. Yonex BG66 Ultimax loses tension relatively quickly — players who string it on Monday often feel a perceptible softening by Wednesday or Thursday. The No. 1's 3D Knit technology interlocks the nylon filaments three-dimensionally, distributing impact stress more evenly and resisting the progressive loosening that affects simpler multifilament constructions at the same gauge. For intermediate to advanced club players who restring every 2–4 weeks, the No. 1 stays crisp and responsive for more of that cycle than the BG66 Ultimax does.

The feel profile demands honest description: the Li-Ning No 1 Badminton String is hard. On contact, the shuttle leaves the string bed quickly and decisively — the feedback is crisp and immediate rather than soft and elastic. Players who have only used thicker strings (BG65, No. 7, VBS 70) will feel the difference dramatically on first use. The hardness is not a flaw — it is what gives the No. 1 its precision and acoustic clarity. Singles players in particular value hard feel for shot calibration: the string bed gives less "forgiveness" on mishits, but rewards precise contact with sharper placement and a more satisfying sound than softer alternatives.

For Indian club players stepping up from BG65 or the Li-Ning No. 7, the Li-Ning No 1 Badminton String represents a substantial quality step: thinner gauge for more repulsion, harder feel for better control feedback, and a professional-level string that genuinely reflects how top players at national and international level string their rackets. At GOS's accessible price, it is one of the best value performance strings on the market for players who are ready for it.
String Character Breakdown of Li-Ning No 1 Badminton String:

0.65mm places the Li-Ning No 1 Badminton String in the performance string category — significantly thinner than the 0.70mm durability standard (BG65, No. 7, VBS 70). Thinner strings produce more repulsion because the string bed deforms more on impact and rebounds faster, launching the shuttle at higher velocity for equivalent swing speed. The trade-off is lower durability — fewer individual fibres means each fibre carries more stress per impact. The No. 1's 3D Knit construction partially compensates for this by improving fibre interlocking, but 0.65mm remains a string for players with consistent technique who can handle the fragility at the sweet spot.
Core — Heat Resistant High-Intensity Nylon Multifilament:

Thousands of individual nylon filaments twisted together form the No. 1's core. Multifilament construction provides the elastic give that generates repulsion — the fibres flex collectively on impact and spring back to launch the shuttle. Heat resistance means the string's properties remain consistent during play sessions where racket temperature rises from sustained impact. High-intensity nylon specification means the fibres are made from a stronger nylon grade with better fatigue resistance per fibre than standard nylon.

The outer layer wraps the multifilament core, protecting the inner structure and providing the contact surface that touches the shuttle. The No. 1's outer is smooth — no texture or coating — which produces the clean, direct feel on contact that characterises the string. Smooth outer surfaces provide less shuttle grip than textured alternatives, meaning the No. 1 prioritises repulsion over spin on net shots and slices.

Li-Ning's proprietary braiding process interlocks the nylon filaments in three dimensions during manufacturing. Standard strings use two-dimensional wrapping; 3D Knit creates more contact points between fibres, distributing impact stress more evenly across the string's cross-section. This makes the No. 1 more durable than other 0.65mm strings without adding gauge — a meaningful advantage for players who want thin string performance without paying the maximum durability penalty of ultra-thin alternatives.

The Li-Ning No 1 Badminton String has a hard feel on contact — the shuttle departs the string bed quickly with minimal dwell time. Hard feel provides crisp, immediate feedback on every shot: the player hears a sharper, higher-pitched sound and feels direct contact through the racket. This characteristic is valued by advanced players for its contribution to shot control and confidence — particularly on smashes and drives where the decisive, instant launch of a hard-feel string produces more penetrating shuttle flight.

A defining advantage over BG66 Ultimax at comparable gauge. The 3D Knit construction and high-intensity nylon resist the progressive tension loss that affects simpler multifilament strings at this gauge. Players who string the Li-Ning No 1 Badminton String at 26–28 lbs find it maintains its crisp playing characteristics meaningfully longer than BG66 Ultimax does at the same tension.
Performance Ratings — Li-Ning No 1 Badminton String:

0.65mm thin gauge delivers very high repulsion — the shuttle launches fast and decisively from the string bed. One of the highest repulsion ratings in the Li-Ning range. Maximum benefit for players with fast, consistent swing technique who can strike near the sweet spot reliably.

Hard feel and precise repulsion give excellent directional feedback on contact. Thin gauge means the effective contact area is smaller — shot placement is more exact. Particularly strong for placement smashes and cross-court drives. Net control is functional but lacks the shuttle-grip of textured strings for fine touch work.

Better than BG66 Ultimax at the same 0.65mm gauge thanks to 3D Knit, but not a durable string by absolute standards. Expect 3–6 weeks for intermediate club players at 24–26 lbs; 1–3 weeks for advanced players at 28+ lbs. Miss-hits and frame contact significantly reduce lifespan. Not for beginners or frequent string-breakers.

Hard, crisp, and decisive — the defining characteristic of the No. 1. Sharp acoustic response (high-pitched, satisfying hitting sound) and direct contact feedback make every shot feel authoritative and controlled. An acquired taste for players transitioning from soft-feel strings, but highly valued by advanced players once adapted.

The accessible tension range for the No. 1 in Indian club conditions. At 22–24 lbs, the string produces the most repulsion with the largest effective sweet spot — good for players transitioning from thicker strings who want the No. 1's repulsion without the unforgiving precision demand of higher tension. At 24–26 lbs, the sweet spot tightens and the acoustic response sharpens — the best all-round tension for most intermediate club players.

The ideal tension range for intermediate-to-advanced competitive players. The No. 1's tension retention advantage over BG66 Ultimax is most clearly felt here — the string holds its crisp, hard feel at this tension for longer between restrings. Placement precision and smash penetration are both enhanced at this range. Most returning professional-level club players using the Li-Ning No 1 Badminton String settle in this bracket.

The tension range used by national and international-level players. At 28–30 lbs, the sweet spot is significantly reduced — consistent technique is non-negotiable. Shuttle response is immediate and decisive. Durability drops sharply; restringing frequency increases. Only appropriate for players who train and compete at a level where string quality genuinely affects competitive outcomes.

The Li-Ning No 1 Badminton String has a 30 lbs maximum. Always verify your racket's stated tension ceiling equals or exceeds your intended string tension before stringing.

name: Yonex Exbolt 68 Badminton String
lines: God of Sports Expert Verdict on Yonex Exbolt 68 Badminton String:

The Yonex Exbolt 68 is the third and most structurally ambitious Exbolt — launched in March 2024 with a specific and surprising identity within the series. Where the Exbolt 63 and 65 lead with Quick Repulsion, the Exbolt 68 leads with Durability. Its most distinctive feature — Oval Forged Fiber — is a structural innovation that has no precedent in Yonex's string range: the cross-section of the Forged Fiber outer transitions from circular (as used in Exbolt 63 and 65) to oval. This geometric change minimises fibre deformation on impact and maximises smash power by redirecting energy into shuttle propulsion rather than absorbing it as fibre deformation. The result, according to Badlab's independent long-term testing: the most durable string in Yonex's entire range — above BG65 despite being 0.68mm rather than 0.70mm.

This durability claim deserves unpacking because it is counterintuitive. BG65 has been the durability benchmark in badminton for decades — a 0.70mm string with special braided fibre designed specifically for abrasion resistance. The Exbolt 68's 0.68mm oval-section Forged Fiber outperforming it in durability is a direct consequence of Forged Fiber's molecular-level bond strengthening. The oval cross-section's reduced deformation per impact means each fibre experiences less mechanical stress per shot — the fibres last longer because they are not being compressed and distorted as much with each contact. Combined with the Elasticity Outer's reduction of inter-string abrasion, the Exbolt 68's total structural durability exceeds what its gauge alone would suggest.

CK Yew's comparative three-string test (Exbolt 68, 65, and 63 on separate rackets at the same 27/29 lbs tension) provides the most honest consumer perspective available: coming from thin repulsion strings, the Exbolt 68 "doesn't provide the immediate repulsion that makes a shuttle scream off the string bed instantly." The Oval Forged Fiber's slightly longer dwell time compared to thin strings is felt as enhanced control and shuttle hold rather than explosive snap-back. This is not a weakness — it is the string's design. The Exbolt 68 is not positioned to compete with the Exbolt 63's snap-back speed; it is positioned to deliver the most durable Exbolt experience with meaningful repulsion for players who are coming from the durability tier (BG65, Nanogy 95, BG80) rather than from the repulsion tier.

Badlab's player targeting is the most precise and useful recommendation: "those who primarily play strings with a larger diameter, such as Yonex Aerobite, Nanogy 95, BG65 or BG80, will find the new Exbolt 68 to be an excellent choice." For Indian players who have been using BG65 and want an upgrade to Forged Fiber's construction quality and repulsion improvement, or who have lost their Nanogy 95 supply due to discontinuation, or who use BG80 Power and want a more comfortable feel with comparable durability — the Exbolt 68 is the targeted recommendation.
String Character Breakdown of Yonex Exbolt 68 Badminton String:

0.68mm places the Exbolt 68 between the Exbolt 65's 0.65mm and BG65's 0.70mm — providing more fibre volume than 0.65mm for durability while being thinner than 0.70mm for meaningful repulsion improvement over durability-only strings. In combination with Oval Forged Fiber, the 0.68mm gauge produces durability that exceeds 0.70mm BG65 — the extra mass is secondary to the structural efficiency of the oval cross-section.
Oval Forged Fiber — The Structural Innovation:

The defining advancement of the Exbolt 68 over the 63 and 65. The circular cross-section of Forged Fiber in Exbolt 63 and 65 compresses relatively easily under perpendicular impact load — circular cross-sections deform in a predictable way under point loads. The oval cross-section resists this deformation more effectively — the oval's longer axis distributes the compression load more efficiently, maintaining its structural geometry under impact. This reduced deformation means: less mechanical fatigue per fibre per impact (longer fibre life), more efficient energy transfer from impact to shuttle propulsion rather than losing energy to fibre deformation (better power-to-deformation ratio), and the most structurally stable Forged Fiber string ever made by Yonex.

The same Elasticity Outer coating as Exbolt 65. Nanoalloy technology adds elasticity and shuttle hold to the surface — increasing dwell time slightly compared to uncoated Forged Fiber (as in Exbolt 63). In the Exbolt 68, the Elasticity Outer's inter-string abrasion reduction works in conjunction with the Oval Forged Fiber's impact deformation resistance to produce a dual-mechanism durability string. The Elasticity Outer also contributes to the comfortable feel — making the Exbolt 68 more accessible than the hard Exbolt 63 despite the Oval Forged Fiber's firmer structural character.

Within the Exbolt series, the 63 and 65 lead with "Quick Repulsion" as their primary claim. The Exbolt 68 leads with "Durability." This is not a lesser string — it is a string for a different player profile: those who value how long a string sustains its performance over how explosive the first contact feels. The repulsion is still meaningfully better than BG65 or Nanogy 95; it is just not the snap-back immediacy of the 0.63–0.65mm Exbolts.

The Oval Forged Fiber's minimised deformation creates slightly longer shuttle contact on the string bed than circular-cross-section alternatives at the same tension. CK Yew notes the Exbolt 68 "holds the shuttle slightly longer than the Exbolt 65 and 63, allowing for enhanced control." This shuttle hold produces a feel that power hitters describe as more satisfying on heavy smashes — the shuttle is felt more deliberately before departure, providing richer tactile feedback on powerful shots.

Vectran is a liquid crystal polymer fibre with tensile strength approximately 5 times greater than steel at equivalent weight. It is an aerospace and industrial material used in demanding structural applications. No other standard Yonex badminton string uses it. When Yonex coils Vectran around the BG80 Power's multifilament core, they are bringing an exceptional engineering material into the string construction — and the results in tension retention, durability, and solid impact feel are measurably distinct from conventional nylon alternatives.

What the BG65 is: a 0.70mm soft-feel durability string with braided nylon construction that provides exceptional abrasion resistance, long-term tension retention, and comfortable extended-session playability. The special braided fibre construction interlocks nylon filaments in a structure that distributes abrasion stress evenly — specifically targeting the notching at cross-string intersections that kills most strings. What the BG65 is not: a repulsion string. The BG65's soft feel and 0.70mm gauge produce adequate repulsion — enough for recreational play, club training, and technique development at all levels.
